- The linked proposal doesn't mention adding this to the ScriptEditor. There are related proposals that also don't mention it either: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11612 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13503#issuecomment-3464212106

Needing the plugin to be open in the internal ScriptEditor loses some of the utility wanted in the proposals. I think this would be better in the FileSystem dock. 

Also the options should only be available for plugins and they should depend on the state of the plugin. Eg. there shouldn't be an option to disable an already disabled plugin.
Makes sense, my idea was for the plugin developer and not the user

It's missing a shortcut to toggle an addon. The menu is an improvement over the current workflow, but it's still not ideal.

Also not sure if having to right-click a specific folder is discoverable.

> It's missing a shortcut to toggle an addon.

How to handle shortcuts for dynamic menu items? Adding the ability to favorite 5 different add-ons and register 5 different shortcuts? "filesystem_dock/toggle_plugin_*"
Or a new shortcut field in the Plugins tab in Project settings?

> Also, not sure if having to right-click a specific folder is discoverable.

I could make it global, so as long as you right-click in the file system, the plugins can be toggled

Well, the proposal already comes with a solution for shortcuts.

> Adding the ability to favorite 5 different add-ons and register 5 different shortcuts?

This is only needed for editor, having that many extra settings is too much I think.
And having one favorite addon means you have to go to project settings and change it when you want to toggle different addon.

> Or a new shortcut field in the Plugins tab in Project settings?

That's overkill, not every plugin needs it, and it isn't useful for regular usage.

> I could make it global, so as long as you right-click in the file system, the plugins can be toggled

So like, adding yet another way to toggle addons?

> Well, the proposal already comes with a solution for shortcuts.

Ok then, I will try the menu under `Editor`

Hey! Thanks for working on this @DexterFstone! 

I think the UX of this can be greatly simplified by avoiding to spawn a submenu, and by simplifying the logic. The most common use case for this toggle will be to enable / disable a single and specific plugin, and I want to make the case that this action alone covers 90% of the proposed feature improvement. Other user actions, such as enabling and disabling multiple plugins at once, are _already_ best done in the player settings plugins window.

So while showing the submenu when you RMB on the addons folder or RMB when you have multiple selected, the added submenu step is IMO unnecessary added complexity.

I propose the following:
- no 'plugins > plugin_name' sub menu.
- when RMB on a folder containing a `plugin.cfg` or on the `plugin.cfg` itself, show an item in the context menu under the folder color item that has a toggle telling it's current active state and with the text 'Enable plugin' (regardless of the state).
- when multiple folders / `plugin.cfg` files are selected, take the enabled state of the plugin you end up RMB on and apply any changes to that state to all other selected plugins, eg: when I select plugin A (disabled) and plugin B (enabled) and plugin C (disabled) and I RMB on plugin A, the toggle will show as off, and clicking Enable plugin will enable all plugins.
- I would suggest not adding any plugin toggle actions to the context menu of the addons folder.

I don't know if Godot even has a third toggle state for checkboxes, but many programs do: where, if you multi-select, instead of showing an empty or checked checkbox, it shows a minus in the checkbox indicating the state is mixed. That would have been ideal for the multi select issue, but if Godot doesn't support that, then we shouldn't bother.

> similar to the proposal

Ah, dang, we are mixing up two different proposals here. I was coming from https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13503#issuecomment-3464212106 which does involve the FileSystem, but if you've moved away from that, this PR won't address that proposal.
Rebase
After rebasing, I got an error

> I don't think this feature is a good idea. I'm not against reloading plugins (I even made a proposal for it: [godotengine/godot-proposals#13503](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13503)) but by adding a menu item called 'Plugins' or whatever, we are creating two places where plugin operations can take place (project settings and in the menu), setting a precedent for moving more options there, and creating the expectation that the checkboxes are some sort of global state.

Well, previously I implemented it like your proposal, but it was rejected

> but by adding a menu item called 'Plugins' or whatever, we are creating two places where plugin operations can take place

Your proposal also do the same thing

> previously I implemented it like your proposal, but it was rejected

I can't find any records of this. Can you elaborate where and why?

> > but by adding a menu item called 'Plugins' or whatever, we are creating two places where plugin operations can take place
> 
> You proposal also do the same thing

It's not the same, mostly because of context: the editor menu items are a global whereas in my proposal I suggest an additional option in the context menu (right mouse button) of a plugin folder or its `plugin.cfg` to enable / disable a plugin. I am not proposing a menu to reload plugins; I am proposing to simply expose the enabled state in the context menu.

But I can guess that you feel like you're being thrown around! That is not my intention. I would just like to avoid scenarios where users start sending in but reports because 'they enabled the plugin through the menu but it doesn't work'.
Menu option doesn't allow for a shortcut (you'd need to have the addon always selected). Having a shortcut was the main idea behind my proposal, so it _should_ be provided in some way.

I personally don't see a UX friendly way of providing a shortcut to reload specific plugins because they will all require 'selecting' plugins and that will inherently conflate with enabling plugins. Perhaps alternatively, a shortcut can be added to the editor that simply reloads all enabled plugins?

But I don't want to reload _all_ plugins :/ It's going to mess up things.

So far my workaround is having a dedicated plugin that reloads plugins, it's just annoying to add it to every project. I guess editor addons will resolve that.

I think the ability to reload plugins is useful to a large part of the Godot users, but to reload specific plugins with an editor shortcut is not. That my usability perspective here. I do think that my proposal is one step closer to the functionality that you desire; instead of an editor shortcut and all the necessary shenanigans that allow you to select which ones get reloaded, you only have to go to the folder in the FileSystem and disable / enable. And not only will that enable a quicker workflow for you, it will also allow people to drop in an addon and immediately enable it in the FileSystem. But I digress; it is true that nothing will be quicker than your plugin to reload what you want, and while this PR implements that, I don't think the potential confusion is worth your fairly niche wish.

Maybe others disagree! I don't mean to push my ideas here. Just sharing why I am not approving it from my perspective.

> I think the ability to reload plugins is useful to a large part of the Godot users, but to reload specific plugins with an editor shortcut is not.

It's mainly useful to plugin developpers, yes. But not having that is like not having F5 to quickly launch the game.

Personally I would agree with adriaan this is more something that should be done in a plugin as it can be done and most users would not benefit from it. 
This looks more like we would need it because we don't have a way to have "editor plugins" or plugins that are added automatically which seems like a bad reasons to add an ux that is as clunky.
Let me make a new alternative for it, so we can decide which one is better
New alternative https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121162
Any chance for someone to look at an alternative?
ok, it seems the alternative is not approved
Well, the above comments pretty much rejected the feature. I proposed and approved it as a tool for plugin creators, but it's not very useful for all/most users.
